match.reason: No single bank point teaches the whole idea of finding unknown angles in reasoned steps across several angle rules and using them to prove parallel lines: the best matches cover only one rule each, and the Year 10 proof point is at a clearly greater depth than Stage 4.

draft.title: Giving reasons for angles
card: To find an unknown angle, work in steps. Write each step as a statement, its working and a reason in brackets. The reason names the angle rule you used.

The reasons you can use are: angles on a straight line add to \(180^{\circ}\), angles at a point add to \(360^{\circ}\), vertically opposite angles are equal, and for parallel lines corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal and co-interior angles add to \(180^{\circ}\).
AOB is a straight line and \(\angle AOC = 110^{\circ}\). Then \(\angle COB = 180^{\circ} - 110^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}\) (angles on a straight line add to \(180^{\circ}\)).
Work backwards. Two lines are parallel if a transversal makes equal corresponding angles, equal alternate angles, or co-interior angles that add to \(180^{\circ}\). State the angles, then the rule.
draft.remember: Every step needs a reason, and an angle pair that fits a parallel-line rule shows the lines are parallel.

a.q: Straight lines AB and CD cross at O. If \(\angle AOC = 70^{\circ}\), which reason gives \(\angle BOD = 70^{\circ}\)?
opts: Vertically opposite angles are equal
Angles on a straight line add to \(180^{\circ}\)
Corresponding angles are equal
Angles at a point add to \(360^{\circ}\)
a.why: \(\angle BOD\) lies directly across the crossing point from \(\angle AOC\), so the two are vertically opposite and equal. Angles on a straight line would give \(110^{\circ}\) for a neighbouring angle, not \(70^{\circ}\) for this one.
a.clue: Where is \(\angle BOD\) compared with \(\angle AOC\)?

b.q: A transversal crosses lines PQ and RS. Between the lines, on the same side of the transversal, the angles are \(112^{\circ}\) and \(68^{\circ}\). What can be said about PQ and RS?
opts: Parallel, as co-interior angles add to \(180^{\circ}\)
Not parallel, as the two angles are unequal
Parallel, as co-interior angles are equal
Parallel, as alternate angles are equal
b.why: These are co-interior angles and \(112^{\circ} + 68^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}\), so the lines are parallel. Unequal angles do not show the lines are not parallel, because co-interior angles on parallel lines are not meant to be equal.
b.clue: Add the two angles and compare with a rule.

b.best: Parallel, as co-interior angles add to \(180^{\circ}\)

problems.detail: Why (b) says co-interior angles on parallel lines are 'not meant to be equal'. They are equal when both are 90°, so this could suggest to students that co-interior angles can never be equal. Better: 'co-interior angles on parallel lines add to 180°, so they need not be equal.'

check.summary: Both questions are correct and match the card. One small issue: why (b) implies co-interior angles on parallel lines cannot be equal, when they are equal if both are 90°.
